land.text: the Tura and Tobol valleys round Tyumen, 'under the White Horde and then the Golden Horde from 1242 to 1468'

predecessors.note: The infobox says 'Preceded by Golden Horde / Uzbek Khanate'. Abu'l-Khayr Khan was crowned in 1428 on the Tura river; his Shaybanid (Uzbek) khanate is not a Cliopatria row (see notes).

land.text: the Tobol, Irtysh and Ob lands taken by the Cossack and Russian forts of 1582-1598 (Qashliq 1582, Tyumen 1586, Tobolsk 1587, Berezov 1593, Surgut and Tara 1594, Narym 1598)

successors.note: Cliopatria's row ends 1587 (Tobolsk); the page ends the khanate in 1598 with Kuchum's defeat at the Irmen near the Ob.

capitals.name: Chimgi-Tura (Tyumen)
capitals.note: Infobox capitals Chimgi-Tura and Qashliq; Abu'l-Khayr was chosen khan on the Tura, 'possibly at Tyumen' (1428).

capitals.name: Sighnaq (Sunaq Ata)
capitals.note: After the 1446 invasion of the Syr Darya 'Sighnaq became his new capital' (Abu'l-Khayr); coordinates approximate. The Taibugid and Shaybanid khans of the north (Mar, Ibak) kept Tyumen.

capitals.name: Chimgi-Tura (Tyumen)
capitals.note: Ibak 'came from Tyumen, where he had been based'; the infobox has him establish Chimgi-Tura as an independent khanate in 1468.

capitals.name: Qashliq (Isker, Sibir)
capitals.note: 'Makhmet moved the capital from Tyumen to Sibir' (undated, about 1495-1496); coordinates approximate (on the Irtysh above Tobolsk). Yermak entered Qashliq on 26 October 1582 (Conquest of Siberia page).

rulers.name: Abu'l-Khayr Khan
rulers.note: Infobox: Khan of Sibir 1428-1468, chosen on the Tura in 1428 at 17; the infobox also lists Hajji Muhammad 1420-1428 as the first ruler, whom Abu'l-Khayr killed after a battle on the Tobol (Abu'l-Khayr page).

rulers.name: Ibak Khan
rulers.note: Infobox 1468-1495; the page dates his killing of the Taibugid Mar to 1464, 1468 or about 1480, and his own death to 1495 (most common), 1494 or 1493.

rulers.name: Mamut
rulers.note: Grandson of Mar, killed Ibak; the end of his reign is not on the pages opened (the Sibir page has Mamuk/Makhmet briefly Khan of Kazan in 1496).

rulers.name: Kuchum
rulers.note: Seized the throne from Yediger and Bekbulat in 1563; defeated on the Irmen in August 1598 and fled to Nogai territory. Yadigar/Yediger (Taibugid) reigned before him (page gives no years).

keyframe_review.note: 3.23 M km2 (11,521 cells): the West Siberian plain from Pelym and the Urals east to Tomsk and the Altai, and the north Kazakh steppe round Astana. The page has Abu'l-Khayr crowned in 1428 on the Tura round Tyumen, then killing Kazhy Mohammed after a battle on the Tobol and being 'proclaimed Khan of Western Siberia'; the Sibir page has the khanate reaching 'the lower Ob in the north' and the Skewbald Horde on the east. No infobox area, so no area comparison; the shape's edges are Cliopatria's. Cliopatria starts 1429, the page's coronation is 1428.

4.37 M km2 (15,353 cells): the 1429 shape plus the steppe of Karaganda, Aqtobe, East Kazakhstan and Qostanay (3,832 cells from nobody). The Abu'l-Khayr page, which the Sibir infobox shares as Khan of Sibir 1428-1468, has him attack Khwarazm in 1430-1431 and 1435-1436 and invade the Syr Darya in 1446; it does not describe the extent of his realm (unverified for the steppe). The shape's southern tip touches Sighnaq. fx-38 (H18): corrected to the 1429 shape. Abu'l-Khayr Khan page: 'Starting in 1446 Abu'l-Khayr and his forces invaded the Syr Darya region', 'The town of Sighnaq became Abu'l-Khayr's new capital'; the Khanate of Sibir page is silent on the steppe, the Syr Darya and Sighnaq. The same realm is drawn in the dedicated Uzbek dossier, and the 1440 shape's Syr Darya edge collided with timurid-empire (134 cells in conflicts.csv, 1440 and 1447).

correction.text: the 1429 shape (Tura, Tobol, Irtysh and lower Ob with the north Kazakh steppe) for 1440-1449; the steppe of Karaganda, Aqtobe, East Kazakhstan and Qostanay (3,832 cells of Cliopatria's 1440 shape, whose southern tip touches Sighnaq) and the Syr Darya are Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek khanate, drawn by uzbek-khanate-of-abul-khayr (steppe 1440, Syr Darya and Sighnaq 1446)

the 1429 shape, valid 1450-1467; the steppe of Karaganda, Aqtobe, East Kazakhstan and Qostanay (3,832 cells of Cliopatria's 1440 shape, whose southern tip touches Sighnaq) and the Syr Darya are Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek khanate, drawn by uzbek-khanate-of-abul-khayr (steppe 1440, Syr Darya and Sighnaq 1446)

keyframe_review.note: Valid 1450-1467: the 1440 extent. Abu'l-Khayr died in 1468 (some sources 1469 or 1470); his steppe realm then breaks away (new keyframe from 1468). fx-38 (H18): the 1429 shape instead of Cliopatria's 1450 shape (which repeats the 1440 steppe).

correction.text: the 1482 shape: West Siberia and the north Kazakh steppe round Astana, without the steppe of Karaganda, Aqtobe and East Kazakhstan, from 1468

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1468-1474: after Abu'l-Khayr's death the Kazakh tribes under Janibek and Kerei, who had 'rejected Abu'l-Khayr's authority', 'settled in what is now Kazakhstan' around 1470 (Kazakh Khanate page), and Ibak holds Sibir from Tyumen. Cliopatria keeps the steppe in the Sibir shape until 1481 and then hands it to the Kazakh Khanate in 1482; the pages place the break in 1468-1470. The corrected shape is Cliopatria's own 1482 shape.

Valid 1475-1481: Ibak Khan (1468-1495) in Sibir; the Cliopatria shape still holds the steppe, which the Abu'l-Khayr and Kazakh Khanate pages place with the Kazakhs and the other Uzbek khans from about 1470.
3.22 M km2 (11,509 cells). Kept: West Siberia with the north Kazakh steppe (Astana, Pavlodar). Ibak's 6 January 1481 victory over Ahmed Khan of the Great Horde moved no frontier on the page.

unverified: page budget. 2.82 M km2 (10,183 cells): Cliopatria hands Aqmola, Pavlodar and Qostanay (1,326 cells) to the Kazakh Khanate in 1487. The Kazakh Khanate page has Burunduk Khan and Muhammad Shaybani divide territory around 1495-1496 (Kazakhs keeping northern Turkestan cities) and says nothing of Sibir or of 1487.
2.82 M km2: unchanged from 1487. Ibak reigns to 1495 from Tyumen.

2.82 M km2: West Siberia between the Tobol and the middle Irtysh with the forest peoples to the north. Mamut/Makhmet takes Ibak's throne about 1495, moves the capital to Sibir (Qashliq) and is briefly Khan of Kazan in 1496 (Sibir and Ibak pages).
2.82 M km2: unchanged. The pages give no territorial event for 1521-1555; the khanate borders Great Perm, the Nogai Horde, the Kazakh Khanate and the Teleuts (Sibir page).

2.82 M km2: unchanged to 1581. Yediger and Bekbulat pay 'limited tribute' to Moscow after 1552; Kuchum seizes the throne in 1563 and stops paying in 1573. Fighting 1556-1563 ended with Yadigar's death.

2.41 M km2 (8,720 cells): Cliopatria drops Tyumen, Qashliq/Tobolsk and the Pelym country (1,460 cells to Russia) in 1582. Yermak entered Qashliq on 26 October 1582 but the Russian forts at Tyumen (1586) and Tobolsk (1587) come later and Kuchum kept attacking submissive tribes to 1595, so the shape is early for Tyumen and Pelym; kept to 1587 as Cliopatria's last shape.

correction.text: the 1582 shape: Kuchum's lands east and south of the Russian forts, held to 1598

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1588-1592: Cliopatria's row ends in 1587, the year of the Tobolsk fort, but the page has Kuchum fighting on and the khanate dissolved only after the Irmen in August 1598. The 1582 shape is kept.

correction.text: the 1582 shape without the Berezov district

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1593: Berezov was founded in 1593 on the lower Ob.

correction.text: the 1582 shape without the Berezov, Surgut and Tara districts

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1594-1597: 'Surgut and Tara were founded in 1594 to protect Tobolsk and subdue the Narym Ostiaks'.

correction.text: the 1582 shape without the Berezov, Surgut, Tara and Narym districts, to the end in August 1598

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1598: Narym was founded in 1598 and Kuchum was defeated at the Irmen near the Ob in August 1598; his family was taken to Moscow and he fled to Nogai territory.

ledger.note: 1428: Abu'l-Khayr Khan is chosen khan on the Tura at Tyumen. 'Released and began consolidating nomadic groups around Tyumen and the Tura River'; the infobox gives 1428 as his coronation for both the Shaybanid Khanate and the Khanate of Sibir (the Sibir page: 'a 17-year-old Shaybanid, Abu'l-Khayr Khan, was chosen Khan on the Tura River, possibly at Tyumen'). The Sibir page's body also says the khanate was 'founded at the end of the 15th century'; I follow the infobox.

region.text: Western Siberia: the Tobol, the Irtysh and the lower Ob, with the north Kazakh steppe

ledger.counterpart: Kazhy Mohammed (Muhammad Khan), khan of Sibir before 1428
ledger.note: 1429: Abu'l-Khayr rules Western Siberia. After a battle on the Tobol he 'deposed and killed Kazhy Mohammed of Sibir' and 'was proclaimed Khan of Western Siberia' (undated; 'the next four years' went to strengthening control). Year inferred from Cliopatria's first shape; the Sibir page has the area under the White and Golden Horde 'from 1242 to 1468' in name only.
1446: the khan's seat moves to Sighnaq on the Syr Darya. 'Sighnaq became his new capital'; coordinates approximate. The northern khans keep Tyumen.

1468: Ibak Khan takes Sibir. The infobox has Ibak Khan establish Chimgi-Tura as an independent khanate in 1468 (reign 1468-1495); the Ibak page dates his killing of the Taibugid Mar to 1464, 1468 or about 1480 with Nogai help. Shaybanid line (Ibak) replaces the Taibugid; same state and colour (rule 2).

region.text: the steppe of Karaganda, Aqtobe, East Kazakhstan and Qostanay, which Abu'l-Khayr had held

ledger.note: 1468-1470: the Kazakh steppe leaves Sibir. Abu'l-Khayr died in 1468 (some sources 1469 or 1470; Abu'l-Khayr page); 'around 1470, the Kazakh tribes, led by Janibek and Kerei, settled in what is now Kazakhstan' after rejecting his authority (Kazakh Khanate page, which dates the khanate 1465). Cliopatria keeps the steppe in the Sibir shape to 1481 and gives it to the Kazakhs in 1482 (3,964 of 3,965 cells). fx-38 (H18): since the steppe is drawn by uzbek-khanate-of-abul-khayr from 1440 (its ledger/7 gives it to the Kazakhs in 1468), this Sibir loss now finds no cells; it stays only to pair with kazakh-khanate ledger/1 until that counterpart is re-pointed to the Uzbek khanate.

region.text: the north Kazakh steppe round Astana, Pavlodar and Qostanay

ledger.note: 1487: Aqmola, Pavlodar and Qostanay pass to the Kazakh Khanate on Cliopatria's map (1,326 cells). Page silent: the Kazakh Khanate page has the Kazakhs and Muhammad Shaybani divide territory about 1495-1496 and names no Sibir frontier; bridging judgment of the date from the shapes.

1495: Mamut kills Ibak and takes Sibir. Ibak 'was killed by Mamut, a grandson of Mar' in 1495 (most common date; 1494 or 1493 elsewhere): the Taibugid line returns; same state (rule 2). The Sibir page gives the killer as Muhammad or Mamuk/Makhmet, who then 'was briefly Khan of Kazan in 1496' (the Ibak page has Mamuk as Ibak's younger brother, a different man).
About 1495-1496: the capital passes from Tyumen to Sibir (Qashliq). 'Makhmet moved the capital from Tyumen to Sibir' (undated; fixed to the year of his accession).

1563: Kuchum seizes the throne. 'In 1563, Kuchum seized the throne from Yediger and Bekbulat' after fighting from 1556 that ended with Yadigar's death; the Shaybanid line returns; same state (rule 2). Yediger and Bekbulat had paid limited tribute to Ivan IV after 1552; Kuchum stopped it in 1573.

region.text: Vogul territory, the Tura and Tobol lands, Qashliq

ledger.note: July 1581: Yermak invades. The conquest 'began in July 1581' when about 540 Cossacks under Yermak invaded Vogul territory; the Stroganov charter of 1574 is not on the page. The zone is the Tura-Tobol country the Cossacks fought through in 1582.

region.text: Vogul territory, the Tura and Tobol lands, Qashliq

ledger.note: 26 October 1582: the Cossacks enter Qashliq. 'The forces of the Khan retreated, and Yermak entered Qashliq on 26 October' after the Battle of Chuvash Cape on 23 October.

1582: Qashliq falls and Kuchum retreats into the steppe. Cliopatria drops the Tobol-Tura lands (Tyumen, Tobolsk, Pelym; 1,460 cells) to Russia in 1582; the page has the forts of Tyumen (1586) and Tobolsk (1587) only later and Kuchum attacking submissive tribes to 1595, so the loss was gradual.
1593: Russia founds Berezov on the lower Ob. 'Berezov was founded in 1593'; the district is my reading of the fort's reach.

region.text: the middle Ob round Surgut and the Irtysh round Tara

ledger.note: 1594: Surgut and Tara are founded. 'Surgut and Tara were founded in 1594, with Surgut and Tara established to protect Tobolsk and subdue the Narym Ostiaks'; the districts are my reading.
1598: Narym is founded on the upper Ob. The timeline lists Narym's founding in 1598 with the conquest of the Piebald Horde.

region.text: Kuchum's remaining Irtysh and Baraba steppe lands

ledger.note: August 1598: Kuchum is beaten at the Irmen. 'Kuchum lost the Battle of Irmen near the Ob River'; the royal family was captured and taken to Moscow; Kuchum fled to the Nogai Horde, then Bukhara, and died in exile around 1605. The Sibir infobox gives 1598 as the year 'conquered by the Tsardom of Russia'.

wars.name: Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Khwarazm and Syr Darya campaigns
wars.outcome: Abu'l-Khayr occupies Urgench in 1430-1431, attacks Khwarazm again in 1435-1436, invades the Syr Darya in 1446 and makes Sighnaq his capital.
wars.note: Urgench was held only briefly (the Uzbeks retreated in summer 1431).

wars.name: Ibak Khan's war against the Great Horde
wars.outcome: Ibak and the Nogai Yamgurchi kill Ahmed Khan of the Great Horde on 6 January 1481; no frontier moves on the page.

wars.name: Kuchum's raids on Perm
wars.outcome: After the Russo-Crimean War of 1571, Kuchum stops paying tribute (1573) and raids the Perm lands.

wars.name: Russian conquest of the Khanate of Sibir (Yermak's campaign)

zones.text: Vogul territory, Tura and Tobol, Qashliq (1581-1582)
the Ob and Irtysh forts of 1593-1598

wars.outcome: Yermak enters Qashliq on 26 October 1582; Cossack and Russian forts follow at Tyumen (1586), Tobolsk (1587), Berezov (1593), Surgut and Tara (1594) and Narym (1598); Kuchum is beaten on the Irmen in August 1598.

certainty.note: A forest, steppe and river realm without surveyed frontiers: the pages name the Tobol, Irtysh, Ishim, Ob and Tura, the lower Ob in the north and the Skewbald Horde to the east. The shapes are Cliopatria's approximate outlines throughout.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Khanate of Sibir' 1429-1587 draws two different things in one colour: (a) the West Siberian khanate of the Tura, Tobol and Irtysh (the shape from 1482 on), and (b) in 1440-1481 also the Kazakh steppe, which was Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Uzbek (Shaybanid) steppe khanate. The Sibir infobox lists Abu'l-Khayr as Khan of Sibir 1428-1468, and the Abu'l-Khayr page also gives him the Shaybanid Khanate (1428-1468, successor Sheikh Haidar). Wikipedia treats the Uzbek/Shaybanid Khanate of Abu'l-Khayr as its own state; Cliopatria has no row for it. I keep one dossier and cut the steppe at 1468 (new keyframe, loss event to kazakh-khanate), but a dossier for the Uzbek Khanate of Abu'l-Khayr (1428-1468, steppe from the Tobol to the Syr Darya, capital Sighnaq from 1446) would belong to the group's additions batch (ia-02-x) or to ia-03 (shaybanids). Its successors would be the Kazakh Khanate (Kerei and Janibek, 1465-1470), Sheikh Haidar's Uzbeks and Sibir.

Tribute: the Sibir page has Yediger and Bekbulat pay 'limited tribute' to Ivan IV after 1552 and Kuchum stop it in 1573 (the 1555 oath is not on the page). The ledger schema has no event for the vassal side, so no vassal_start/end is written here; the tsardom-of-russia dossier (eu-16) should carry vassal_start 1552 / vassal_end 1573 with counterpart khanate-of-sibir.

Disagreements between pages: (1) the Sibir body says the khanate was founded 'at the end of the 15th century', the infobox starts 1428; (2) the Ibak page dates Ibak's killing of Mar to 1464, 1468 or about 1480, and his own death 1493, 1494 or 1495; (3) Mamuk/Makhmet/Mamut: the Sibir page has Makhmet (Mamuk) kill Ibak, the Ibak page has Mamut, a grandson of Mar, kill him and Mamuk as Ibak's younger brother; (4) the Sibir page puts Kuchum's last defeat 'on the banks of the Ob' in 1598, the conquest page 'near the Ob' (Irmen), August 1598.

Unverified, page budget (5 pages) used: the extent of the khanate to the north and east (Yamal, Tomsk, Altai) is Cliopatria's; the 1487 hand-over of Aqmola, Pavlodar and Qostanay; the districts of the 1593-1598 forts (radii are my reading); the date of the move of the capital to Qashliq; Kazan 1496 is Mamuk's, not a Sibir gain.

Gazetteer names needed: Sighnaq, Berezovo, Tara, Narym, Pelym, Qashliq (Isker); coordinates are given as lon/lat in the dossier. 'Western Siberia' exists.

End year: the dossier ends in August 1598 (Irmen) as the Sibir infobox does; Cliopatria's last shape is 1587. Keyframes 1588-1598 are new.
